package.description: Live battery monitoring for wireless mice, keyboards, headsets and controllers on Windows.

en-US.description: Live battery monitoring for wireless mice, keyboards, headsets and controllers on Windows.
en-US.longDescription: Battery Hub reads the battery level of wireless HID peripherals — mice, keyboards, headsets and game controllers — and shows them on a single dashboard with a per-device indicator in the system tray and low-battery notifications. Devices with no known protocol can be set up through a guided calibration wizard that identifies which byte of the HID report carries the battery level, so support is not limited to a fixed list of models. Runs entirely locally and collects no user data.
en-US.name: Battery Hub
en-US.releaseNotes:
Battery Hub now knows when a wireless device is switched off, and reads more devices correctly.
Fixed
- A wireless device switched off while its receiver stayed plugged in, such as a Logitech G502 X, kept showing its last level as if it were still on. It now shows Asleep or off (Turned off for headsets), keeps its last level dimmed, and comes back by itself. This works for VXE and ATK mice, Logitech, Razer, SteelSeries, HyperX, Corsair, MCHOSE and Audeze devices and PlayStation controllers.
- Mice nap a few seconds after you stop moving them, so a mouse or keyboard keeps its normal look until it hasn't answered for 2 minutes.
- A switched-off SteelSeries Aerox or Prime mouse showed 0%, and a DualShock 4 adapter with no controller on it showed 5%.
- A Razer device, or one set up with a scan, didn't read again after its receiver was unplugged and plugged back in, until Battery Hub restarted.
- With Logitech G HUB running, its traffic could be mistaken for a Logitech mouse's or headset's answer.
- A Compx receiver that refuses requests on its usual channel is now tried on its other channels.
